name: The Covenant of Works and Original Righteousness

objectives.text: Identify that God made Adam and Eve good and without sin when he placed them in the garden
Name the one command God gave Adam about the tree of the knowledge of good and evil
Describe the good gifts God gave Adam in the garden, including food from every other tree, the tree of life, and work to do
Recall that God warned Adam that eating from the forbidden tree would bring death
Explain that God's command in the garden tested whether Adam would trust and obey him
Define a covenant as a relationship God establishes with promises, conditions, and consequences
Explain original righteousness as the uprightness Adam and Eve had at creation, with God's law written on their hearts and the power to obey it
Summarize the covenant of works as the Reformed tradition confesses it, in which life was promised to Adam and his descendants on condition of perfect and personal obedience
Identify the parties, condition, promise, and penalty of the covenant of works in Genesis 2
Explain why the tradition teaches that Adam was created able to keep God's law yet able to fall
Interpret the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil as signs of the covenant of works
Compare the covenant of works with the covenant of grace in their conditions, mediator, and promises
Analyze Adam's role as covenant head who represented all humanity in the covenant of works
Explain the confessional teaching that the want of original righteousness belongs to the sinfulness of humanity after the Fall
Analyze the biblical evidence, including Hosea 6:7, that God's arrangement with Adam was a covenant even though Genesis 2 does not use the word
Explain how the broken covenant of works shows that fallen sinners cannot gain life by the law and so need Christ
Explain how the moral law given to Adam as a covenant of works continues after the Fall as a perfect rule of righteousness
Explain how Christ as the last Adam fulfilled through his active and passive obedience what Adam failed to do
Explain why the Westminster Confession grounds the covenant of works in God's voluntary condescension rather than in any creature's strict merit
Trace the development of the doctrine of the covenant of works in Reformed theology from the sixteenth century through the Westminster Standards
Evaluate denials of a pre-Fall covenant using Scripture and the arguments of Reformed theologians
Defend the Reformed teaching that the imputation of Adam's guilt runs parallel to the imputation of Christ's righteousness
Compose a theological essay that traces the two covenant heads through Scripture, showing ruin in Adam and righteousness in Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (sinless creation, the one command, the death warning, summary of the covenant, original righteousness, comparison with grace, Adam's headship, the trees as signs, Christ's active obedience, evaluating denials, imputation parallel, two-heads synthesis). Dropped the vague 'apply' and 'construct a theology' items and merged the duplicate Christ-as-last-Adam entries. Added the definition of covenant, the garden gifts, the command as test, the parts of the covenant, Adam's mutability, Hosea 6:7 evidence, loss of original righteousness, the moral law's continuance, voluntary condescension, and the doctrine's historical development. Moved the creation of the image to its sibling sub-topic and kept only original righteousness here. Updated confession citations to full document names and added WSC Q10, Q12, Q16, Q18, WLC Q20, Q25, Q30, and WCF 6.3, 7.1, 9.2, 11.1, 19.1-2, 19.6.
